heading: CHAPTER XXVI.
title: AN EXHORTATION TO LIBERATE ITALY FROM THE BARBARIANS
exclusions: front matter and dedication before THE PRINCE
notes: Chapter 26 is the book's final synthesis. The exhortation is not separate patriotic ornament but the point at which classification, military argument, opportunity, and founding all converge.

Machiavelli combines providential rhetoric, public suffering, great willingness, and a direct address to the Medici house with the same practical conditions the book has stressed throughout: own arms, new laws, and leadership able to give order to existing courage.

Italy's problem is not lack of raw valour. The country has valour in the limbs but fails in the head, so willingness alone is insufficient without a directing founder, a new order, and forces of its own.
